missing_requested_row: NET-98 is absent from both the ownership map and the live inventory. No row created.
excluded_row: NET-68 belongs to NET_IMPL and was not edited.
result: Precise gaps and acceptance plan only. No completed rows or new tests.

rows.behavior: `nextwave`: host, Horde, not paused: ends the current break.
rows.gap: Horde next-wave control is outside the approved two-human Conquest profile.

rows.behavior: `end`: host in play: result `{ended:true}`, back to the lobby, offline humans freed.
rows.gap: Host end is in the unavailable command list. Do not add a lifecycle control under this task.

rows.behavior: Per-seat units: own and allied units, plus enemies in team vision; planes only while airborne; everything during the end reveal.
rows.gap: Full unit visibility, plane and end-reveal matrix requires a separate producer/privacy acceptance plan.

rows.behavior: Row privacy for non-owners: cooldown 0, flags masked to bits 0-10, 15, 18, 20-22 (drops stances, autocast, gate-open, operative, cargo bits); target id 0 unless the receiver sees the target.
rows.rust_requirement: Same mask on cached rows (see open questions on the dropped bits).
rows.unreal_requirement: Never expect hidden bits on others' rows.
rows.gap: Non-owner flag/target policy has pending owner decisions. No mask change is authorized.

rows.behavior: Owner-only lists: movement, queues, productionJobs, plans, orders, rally, air, sup, mp, inc, mun, fuel, fuelInc, upkeep, tech, logistics.
rows.rust_requirement: Build them for the receiving seat only.
rows.unreal_requirement: HUD reads them for the local seat only.
rows.gap: Complete owner-only field families depend on gameplay producers outside the four admitted input families.

rows.behavior: Team-scoped data: covers, works, ghosts (remembered enemy buildings not seen now), foundMines; scenario objectives and `say` shots by recipient policy.
rows.gap: Team memory, engineering and scenario recipient policies are outside this server lifecycle batch.

rows.behavior: Terrain: `start` carries the receiver's whole remembered terrain; snapshots carry only remembered cells changed since the last one (pending until seen; unseen footprints and hidden mines stay pending). World uses the team memory and its change log.
rows.gap: Terrain ownership and delivery changes are explicitly excluded by this task.

rows.behavior: Fog: `start` sends `{v, e}` run strings (seen now, ever seen); snapshots send one run string of flipped cells only when team vision changed; non-World spectators get no fog.
rows.unreal_requirement: Decode runs; XOR deltas onto the seen mask.
rows.gap: Fog producer and spectator branch need their own complete acceptance; no spectator expansion here.

rows.behavior: Regular shots use visible position, allied or seen participants, or public status outside World; hidden unit IDs are removed. Local projectile events and live flights require visible ground fog, and hidden IDs lose paired owner fields. Event launch extrapolation is fog-bounded; live flight extrapolation also reads actual contact facts.
rows.unreal_requirement: Play effects only from received shots.
rows.gap: Shot and live-flight privacy predicates require the complete combat producer matrix and privacy agreement.

rows.behavior: Smokes, fires and falling sections only where the team sees; World strikes only allied or seen; strikes in other modes are public.
rows.gap: Environment effects and World strike privacy are outside this bounded Conquest socket batch.

rows.behavior: Contested flag on a point only when the receiver sees units of two teams on it.
rows.acceptance: port CACHE (line 6758: contest kept for a player who sees it).
rows.gap: Point contest visibility is a gameplay recipient predicate; do not revise its policy here.

rows.behavior: End reveal: `finish()` sets `g.reveal`, so every receiver sees every unit during the 6 s hold.
rows.gap: Complete end reveal depends on full unit visibility and terminal scenarios; partial Conquest hold evidence is insufficient.

rows.behavior: AI seats see the same seat view without the browser fog mask (`omitFogMask`).
rows.gap: AI seats are not admitted in R1; no AI view consumer is enabled by this task.

rows.behavior: Snapshot cache built once per send and shared; per-receiver filtering never mutates shared rows; cached output equals an uncached build.
rows.gap: Cache equivalence needs the complete supported recipient/field matrix, not the current two-seat smoke checks.

rows.behavior: Unit deltas (`unitDelta`): per receiver `sent` map; changed rows only, `gone` ids, `all` when full, `held` = [count, xor of ids].
rows.rust_requirement: Same algorithm per seat, operative and spectator stream.
rows.acceptance: port HELD (every room test asserts it).
rows.gap: Seat delta producer and a two-seat resync socket witness exist. Complete row acceptance also requires changed-only/gone/order/held checks through real delivery and operative/spectator streams, which R1 does not admit.

rows.behavior: `wrecks` and `nodes` resent only on change: outside World a room-level version per cache; in World a per-receiver JSON compare. Omitted means "unchanged".
rows.rust_requirement: Same omission rule (see the stale-wrecks question).
rows.unreal_requirement: Keep the last list when absent.
rows.acceptance: new test: a list is absent until it changes, present after.
rows.gap: Shared and personal list trimming have fixture consumers. No complete real-socket list-change/omission witness was found in the inspected socket tests; World personal streams are outside R1. Preserve the documented late-discovery stale-wreck question.

rows.behavior: Every snapshot carries `online` (connected or AI per seat) and `ping` (rtt per seat, -1 for AI, null unknown).
rows.acceptance: new test: values after a disconnect.
rows.gap: send_native_frame derives online only from Connection::ready and ping only from Person.rtt. Source also requires AI online=true and ping=-1. Native attachment rejects AI. Existing human snapshots are partial coverage, not the complete row.

rows.behavior: `resync` in play marks the sender's delta record full (spectator stream outside World); the next snapshot has `all`. Client sends it at most once a second when `held` disagrees.
rows.acceptance: new test: corrupt client rows, expect `resync` then `all`.
rows.gap: The requester account is marked full and a two-seat socket test checks all=true without making the peer full. It does not deliberately lose a decoded row or prove the client one-second resync throttle. Spectator resync is outside R1.

rows.behavior: Snapshots are built only for open sockets (readyState 1) and only when someone can receive them.
rows.gap: select_native filters Connection::ready; collect_frame and send_native_frame handle selected seats. Existing socket checks show delivery to live seats, but do not pin no-recipient producer nonexecution or a closing-socket boundary. A new controlled real-socket witness is needed.

rows.behavior: Tick clock: 20 Hz sim; a 10 ms poll runs the ticks `hrtime` says are due, at most 4 per poll; a longer stall drops the backlog.
rows.acceptance: new test: a 1 s stall runs 4 ticks, then resumes on schedule.
rows.gap: CatchUpClock and its fixture cover the one-second stall and four-tick cap. Hub::poll_native consumes it, but the fixture uses a counter in place of rooms and has no sockets. Need explicit-clock Hub polling with actual connected recipients; elapsed-time sleeps cannot prove exact boundaries.

rows.behavior: Per-room tick order: expiry, skip if not playing or still starting, pause tick, `away` flags, end hold, timed tick, World autosave, diag. Rooms run one after another in one process.
rows.gap: The complete tick-order row includes World autosave and diagnostics, outside R1.

rows.behavior: Snapshot cadence: send when `tick % snapEvery == 0` or a winner exists; snapEvery starts at 2; checked each second after 10 samples: p95 of the last 50 snapshot ticks over 40 ms adds 1 (max 4); under 24 ms for 10 s removes 1 (min 2).
rows.gap: TickMeter fixtures cover thresholds, ring windows and recovery; RoomRuntime consumes the meter. No complete deterministic socket witness ties every emitted frame to the source-recorded cadence changes and winner override. Do not introduce artificial measured durations into production.

rows.behavior: AI seats and the Horde seat think on the shared schedule and see only the last delivered snapshot beat.
rows.rust_requirement: Same coupling of AI view to delivery.
rows.gap: AI and Horde scheduling/delivery consumers are outside R1.

rows.behavior: Seat backpressure: skip a seat while 256 KiB or more is in flight (counted until the write callback); when it drains, send one catch-up snapshot (no shots or cells).
rows.gap: SeatBackpressure and write-completion routing exist. The original socket test uses controlled inflight accounting, but native component fixture replay alone does not prove real transport skip/drain, exactly one catch-up, empty shots/cells or unchanged skipped delivery history.

rows.behavior: Spectator drop: a spectator socket with more than 4 MiB buffered is closed with 1013 "too far behind".
rows.unreal_requirement: Reconnect and rebuild from the next full snapshot.
rows.gap: R1 rejects spectators; a watcher threshold helper is not a live spectator socket consumer.

rows.behavior: Spectator streams: outside World one shared stream (one build, one string, shared terrain memory `g.watchPending`), made full when a spectator starts; World spectators get their own stream from seat 0's team memory.
rows.gap: R1 has neither shared ordinary spectators nor World spectator streams.

rows.behavior: Spectator content: seat 0's start; outside World the fog is lifted (every unit, no mask); seat-private keys removed, seat 0's cooldowns and stance bits cleared, public objectives and shots only.
rows.unreal_requirement: Spectator mode: no orders, whole map outside World.
rows.gap: Spectator content/admission and privacy require owner agreement; this task cannot choose them.

rows.behavior: End hold: once a winner exists the room stays in play 6 s (120 ticks), stepping every other tick and sending a frame each step; AIs idle; orders refused. Then outcomes per seat and the lobby with the result (winner, teams, names, story fields, Horde part).
rows.gap: Complete Source END includes AI and broader terminal result families; the current Conquest path is partial evidence.

rows.behavior: Host `pause`/`resume` in play. While paused: no sim, AI or commands, no operative input; the pause message plus one frame go out once a second.
rows.gap: Host pause/resume are unavailable network commands. Any new lifecycle input needs scope agreement.

rows.behavior: Auto-pause on a human drop in play: 30 s, once per player per match; ends on reconnect, AI handover, deadline or host resume. (A loaded save opens with a `host` pause instead, NET-92.)
rows.gap: Drop pause and same-token resume are wired and have socket witnesses. Full Source checks also need exact deadline, per-player once-per-match/reset behavior, AI handover and host resume. R1 disallows AI and the current dispatcher refuses resume/handAi.

rows.behavior: Pause message `{paused, by, reason, left}` sent on every change, on join during a pause, and every second while paused.
rows.gap: Drop pause wire fields and join ordering are present. Complete checks of left at 30/24/1/0, periodic message/frame ordering, host pause and resume are missing. Host pause/resume commands remain unavailable; extending them is outside this frozen plan.

rows.behavior: Socket close: a seat stays (lobby: freed after 10 s unless the same token returns; play: offline until the end); a spectator is removed at once and never pauses; an operative is marked offline.
rows.gap: Complete row includes spectator and operative close lifecycles, outside R1.

rows.behavior: Match end frees offline humans; the result's per-seat lists (teams, names, story) follow seats as they are freed or added.
rows.unreal_requirement: Report rows stay with their player.
rows.gap: Full result row movement requires result families and seat changes beyond the fixed R1 roster.

rows.behavior: A player's own outcome: `lastMatch` per seat (victory, defeat, draw), sent as `result.you` in that player's lobby.
rows.gap: Complete Source END outcome checks include AI and non-Conquest results; preserve current limited evidence.

rows.behavior: Latency ping: client sends `{t:'ping', c, rtt, d}` every 2 s; server stores rtt clamped 0-9999 and replies `{t:'pong', c}` plus `srv:[p95 ms, snapEvery]` during play. Never relayed.
rows.unreal_requirement: Send every 2 s; show ping, loss, server numbers.
rows.gap: Native pong omits the Source in-play srv pair. Adding it would change wire output and is excluded.

rows.behavior: Map ping `{t:'ping', x, z}`: seated human in play, finite and inside the map, 3 per 5 s per player (invalid ones do not use the budget); relayed as `{t:'ping', from, x, z}` (0.1 m) to connected human teammates including the sender.
rows.unreal_requirement: Alt+click sends; ring 4 s with alert.
rows.gap: Native ping handling returns without map-ping dispatch when x or z exists. Complete map-ping policy is not implemented here.

rows.behavior: Client reconnect: backoff 1, 2, 4, 8, 8 s with a countdown; reset after any server message; after `full` retry every 10 s; `replaced` stops retrying; events from an older socket are ignored.
rows.acceptance: port RL@5647 (lines 5659-5725) against the Unreal connection class.
rows.gap: Unreal reconnect/backoff is client-owned; this stream cannot deliver its runtime consumer.

rows.behavior: Client identity: token per room (plus optional `&seat=` suffix; operatives use `<seat or fps>-<commander>`) in local and session storage; camera, selection and groups saved per token and restored when a `start` has the same matchId.
rows.acceptance: port RL@5647 (lines 5726-5757); live: refresh mid-match keeps camera.
rows.gap: Unreal identity/storage/camera restoration is client-owned; this stream cannot deliver its runtime consumer.

rows.behavior: Manual save: host in play; reply `{t:'saved', id}` and a lobby update, or `deny {cmd:'save',reason:'save'}`. Only one save at a time per room.
rows.gap: Manual save remains explicitly unavailable; persistence implementation is outside R1.

rows.behavior: Autosave: World Conquest only, every 2 minutes of play (2,400 ticks) while undecided.
rows.acceptance: new test: autosave appears after 2,400 ticks.
rows.gap: World autosave requires an admitted World runtime and persistence, outside R1.

rows.behavior: Save storage: V8-serialized `{g, guard (players[-1]), map (null in World), seats, settings, ai}` gzipped to `<room>-<ms>-<kind>.save` (via `.tmp` then rename) plus a `.json` summary; newest 3 auto and 10 manual kept per room; dir `SAVES_DIR` (default `saves/`).
rows.rust_requirement: Same layout and retention; format is an open question.
rows.acceptance: port test-saves.mjs:15-28 (round trip plays on identically).
rows.gap: Persistence format is an open contract question; V8 compatibility is not silently replaced.

rows.behavior: Load: host in lobby, id valid and prefixed with the room code. Settings restored; seats go back by token, else to the next connected human, else wait offline; other present humans become spectators; AI memories restored; human seats get fresh AI helpers; the match opens paused by the host. Failure: `deny {cmd:'loadSave',reason:'save'}`.
rows.rust_requirement: Same seat matching and paused start.
rows.unreal_requirement: Saves list with Load for the host.
rows.gap: loadSave is unavailable, and complete loading includes AI/role transitions outside R1.

rows.behavior: Lobby `saves`: this room's saves, newest first (id, kind, savedAt, mode, minutes, names, world).
rows.gap: Complete save-list acceptance depends on a real persistence writer/reader.

rows.behavior: Horde records: best run per `map|team size|army` (higher wave, then longer time) in `horde-records.json`; `result.horde` {wave, kills, time, names, record, best}; lobby `hordeBest`; sandbox runs not recorded; shards send runs to the front, which writes the file.
rows.gap: Horde records and cross-process record ownership are outside the approved profile.

rows.behavior: Sandbox: lobby flag reaches `start.sandbox`; the `spawn` command works only in sandbox games, no structures, at most 2,000 units, `enemy` gives the unit to the enemy or the Horde.
rows.unreal_requirement: Sandbox panel (unit, side, click to spawn).
rows.acceptance: port test.js:7390 "Sandbox spawns any unit for either side".
rows.gap: R1 requires sandbox off; no spawn input expansion is authorized.

rows.behavior: Shards: `WW2_SHARDS=N` (1-64) makes a front that serves HTTP, merges `/api/rooms` from game processes and replays each `/ws` upgrade to process FNV-1a(code) mod N; other upgrade paths are destroyed; a dead game process restarts after 1 s; game processes exit when the front goes. IPC: `ready {port}`, `record {key, run}`, `maps`.
rows.rust_requirement: Room routing by code to one worker (threads or processes, open question).
rows.gap: Worker/shard topology and IPC are outside this single-process R1 task.

rows.behavior: Diagnostics: `WW2_DIAG=1` writes a JSON line per playing room every 5 s to `logs/diag-<room>.jsonl` (tps, lateness, loop delay, tick p50/p95, snapEvery, per player rtt, quiet ms, buffered bytes, clamped browser numbers from ping `d`). `WW2_TICKLOG=1` logs phase p50/p95 every 30 s.
rows.gap: Private R1 admission/fault receipts do not supply the Source periodic diagnostics and browser-metric recorder.
